songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy ’68 set with blazing Morning Dew and expansive Dark Star
ai_show_review.blurb: The Columbus Veterans Hall show delivers a scorching Morning Dew and a marathon Dark Star that capture the band at peak intensity. New Potato Caboose and the The Other One → Cryptical Envelopment suite add depth to an otherwise raw, audience‑only recording. Despite muddy fidelity, the performance remains a vivid snapshot of late‑1968 Dead power.
ai_show_review.review: The November 22, 1968 Columbus Veterans Hall concert finds the Dead in full‑blown improvisational mode. Jerry’s guitar is on fire from the opening chords of Morning Dew through an unrelenting Dark Star that stretches into the second half of the set, while Phil’s bass underpins the chaos despite being buried in the tape’s haze. The band weaves a seamless suite—Saint Stephen into The Eleven, then into Turn On Your Lovelight—before diving into the double‑Cryptical Envelopment/Other One sequence, culminating in a gritty New Potato Caboose that showcases their willingness to push boundaries. Mickey Hart carries all percussion duties on the first tape, delivering a driving groove that compensates for Bill’s absence; Pigpen’s organ and harmonica are barely audible through the audience mic, but his presence is felt in the overall texture. Though the recordings are far from pristine, the raw energy and daring improvisations make this show an essential listen for fans of the Dead’s late‑summer ’68 era.

best_recording.reason: Fair‑quality audience tape with a slightly clearer mix and later remaster that adds warmth, making the high‑energy performance more listenable than the poorer alternative.

key_highlights: Blazing Morning Dew that showcases Jerry’s incendiary lead work
Extended Dark Star jam that captures the band’s late‑’68 improvisational peak
The Other One → Cryptical Envelopment suite with tight transitions
New Potato Caboose adds a gritty, experimental edge despite limited keyboard audibility

band_performance.Jerry: Guitar is snarling and on fire, especially during Morning Dew and Dark Star, cutting through the muddy mix.
band_performance.Phil: Solid bass foundation that drives the jams, though often obscured by recording limitations.
band_performance.Mickey: Handles all drum duties on the first tape, providing a powerful, driving groove throughout.
band_performance.Billy: Absent from this show; his usual rhythmic interplay is missing.
